title: Headroom-first Autoscaler: throughput targets, slew limiting, and safety fences for Dedicated fleets
creator: Samir Patel
description: Define and implement a headroom-first autoscaling policy for Dedicated GPU fleets that targets throughput guarantees while enforcing conservative safety fences. The goal is to support tenant-level committed throughput in bursty traffic patterns without violating latency SLOs or causing cascading capacity churn across the fleet.
acceptance_criteria: Autoscaler produces scaling decisions that maintain configured per-tenant committed throughput >= 95% during simulated 1h burst windows
P95 tail latency stays within SLA target for 99% of requests during burst scenarios
No more than 10% of scaling actions are rollbacks due to safety fence violations in 48h production-like replay
Scaling decisions respect max surge (configurable) and global fleet headroom budget
Observed cost delta for representative workload is within expected estimate (+/-10%) when using headroom strategy vs baseline PID scaler
design_notes: Primary signal: tenant_target_throughput (tokens/sec committed) + observed_request_rate (requests/sec) + GPU_utilization
Secondary signals: KV_cache_hit_rate, avg_sequence_length, queue_depth, recent_rejection_rate

Control strategy: hierarchical controller combining a headroom allocator for reserved capacity, a model-based proportional-integral term tuned to slow variability, and a surge-credit reservoir for short bursts
Slew limiting: enforce per-fleet and per-tenant slew limits (max delta percent per 5m window) to prevent cascading reallocations
Safety fences: max_surge_pct, cooldown_window, rollback_score_threshold, and tenant_fairshare_weighting
Allocation policy: prefer warm lanes with KV-affinity when scaling up; when scaling down prefer emptying cold lanes first
Quantization: translate continuous capacity target to integer instance counts with hysteresis to avoid flip-flop around boundaries
Edge cases: graceful fallback to compatible model variant if capacity cannot be provisioned within cooldown_window
implementation_plan: 1) Prototype headroom allocator library (golang) that computes per-tenant headroom targets from committed throughput and recent usage patterns
2) Implement surge-credit reservoir and API to debit/credit bursts per tenant; integrate with billing ledger for accounting
3) Extend autoscaler decision graph to include safety fence evaluation and rollback scoring
4) Add KV-affinity hints to node placement planner and warm-lane prioritizer
5) Add metric exports and dashboards for headroom utilization, rollback_rate, and surge_credit_balance
6) Run offline replay tests, chaos injection, and final canary rollout to a small Dedicated pool
progress_updates: 2026-02-18: Spike complete — simulated headroom allocator in python; initial heuristics look reasonable for median workloads (Samir)
2026-02-22: Design review with PLT — accepted hierarchical controller approach; asked to add explicit rollback scoring (Liam Park)
2026-02-26: PR #7342 created for reservoir API and ledger schema; tests added for debit/credit invariants (Aisha)
2026-03-01: Benchmarks against baseline PID scaler show 12% reduction in stray scale-ups but 4% higher steady-state cost in synthetic steady workloads (Marta Silva)
2026-03-04: Implemented per-tenant slew limiter and added cooldown_window enforcement; integration tests failing intermittently under high-load replay (investigating)
comments: Liam Park (2026-02-22): Add a deterministic rollback scoring function so we can reason about 'why' a scale decision was reversed. Consider using weighted signals with time-decayed contributions.
Marta Silva (2026-02-28): Performance numbers look good. Need an experiment that compares end-to-end latency and cold-start costs when warm-lane affinity is enforced vs not.
Jordan Lee (2026-03-03): Watch out for cross-tenant noisy neighbor effects when surge-credit is exhausted; propose a global soft-cap to protect system SLOs.
Aisha Khan (2026-03-04): Test flakiness traced to race condition in node decommission path when cooldown_window is short. Created follow-up ENG-31500 to harden decommission flow.
test_plan: Unit tests for allocator math and quantization
Integration tests with node-placer that verify KV-affinity warm-lane selection
Offline replay across historical 30-day trace set with stochastic bursts and tenant mixes
Chaos tests: fail nodes during scale-up, inject high-latency network partitions
Canary: roll to 2 Dedicated pools representing low and medium-traffic tenants for 72h with tight alerting
rollout_strategy: Stage 1: internal dedicated dev pool (non-customer) for 48h
Stage 2: select low-risk customer tenants (opt-in) for 72h
Stage 3: broad rollout by tenant cohorts with guardrail thresholds tightened gradually
Rollback: automated if rollback_rate > 10% or if any tenant experiences SLA violation > 1% in canary window
risks: Overprovisioning steady-state when headroom targets are conservative, increasing cost
Race conditions between decommission and reallocation paths causing transient request failures
Surge-credit exhaustion leading to unexpected throttling for bursty tenants
Complexity makes debugging scaling incidents slower for on-call engineers
Incorrect KV-affinity heuristics could create imbalanced node packing
